turns.learner: Hello! Can you give me an exercise on at, on and in for time?
turns.tutor:
Use at with clock times, on with days and dates, in with months and years.
Right: "The film starts at six o'clock."
Wrong: "The film starts in six o'clock." Six o'clock is a clock time, so in is wrong.
My example: "The zoo is closed on Saturday." Saturday is a day, so I use on.
Now you. Write in, on or at:
My train leaves ___ 5 o'clock.
